MaxInitialHp.rationale: Axebot.cs:46 GetValueIfAscension(ToughEnemies, 86, 78) -> 78. The one unit in this batch with a genuine HP RANGE, so the roll matters; the roll itself is monsters/base.py's, not this unit's.

AfterAddedToRoom.rationale: SHARED-FINDINGS section 2's shared verdict, copied not re-derived. The sim has no add-to-room phase -- creature creation *is* construction -- so AfterAddedToRoom's effect is applied from __init__ (axebot.py:48-51, `if stock > 0: PowerCmd.apply(hooks, self, StockPower, stock)`). Same observable today on all three clauses: (a) listener set -- the only ported listeners on the hooks a starting power can reach are relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38, relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53, relics/vambrace.py:26-40 and relics/paels_legion.py:36-43, and all four gate on `target is self.player` / `applier is self.player` / `card is not None`, which a self-applied cardless starting power cannot satisfy; (b) HP-roll inversion -- only IllusionPower mentions max_hp and only inside revive() (powers.py:1581); (c) roll ordering -- `py audit/tools/monster_probes.py roll-order` shows all 29 machine sites are sticky-no-op. Rule 7: that rationale cites four relic files and powers.py which this record does NOT hash. Concrete trigger that would make it a gap: any relic/potion/power listening on modify_power_amount / on_power_applied / modify_block_* without gating on the player, or a starting power whose amount reads owner.max_hp. Escalation check: self-applied, reads nothing from hooks.combat -- shared verdict fits. The `StockAmount > 0` guard (Axebot.cs:78) is reproduced exactly (axebot.py:48), and `StockAmount` is `_stockOverrideAmount ?? 2` (Axebot.cs:50-61) = the sim's `stock: int = _DEFAULT_STOCK` default (axebot.py:20, :42). Note Axebot.cs:76-82 does NOT call `base.AfterAddedToRoom()`, which is harmless: the base is a no-op (MonsterModel.cs:313-316).

GenerateMoveStateMachine (protected; add.rationale: The GRAPH is exact and the INITIAL-STATE PREDICATE is expressed differently. Axebot.cs:84-100 builds BOOT_UP_MOVE, ONE_TWO_MOVE and HAMMER_UPPERCUT_MOVE with boot_up->hammer, hammer->one_two, one_two->hammer; axebot.py:66-68 is identical, same ids, same registration list order [boot_up, one_two, hammer]. BOOT_UP is therefore only ever an initial state, never re-entered, on both sides. The initial state is chosen by `if (_stockOverrideAmount.HasValue) -> BOOT_UP else -> HAMMER_UPPERCUT` (Axebot.cs:95-99): a bot whose Stock was set explicitly (a respawn) boots up, the fight's first bot swings. The sim splits that into a separate `respawn: bool` keyword (axebot.py:43, :46, :69). Same observable, EXECUTED over both ported call sites rather than asserted: the encounter constructs `Axebot(hooks, rng)` with NEITHER keyword (axebot.py:92-95, AXEBOTS_NORMAL), giving stock=2/respawn=False -> HAMMER, matching C#'s null override -> HAMMER; and the only other constructor call in the whole sim is StockPower.on_death's `Axebot(self.hooks, combat._rng, stock=self.amount - 1, respawn=True)` (powers.py:2978-2982), which sets BOTH, giving BOOT_UP, matching C#'s `StockAmount = base.Amount - 1` setter (StockPower.cs:23) -> HasValue -> BOOT_UP. The two predicates coincide at every reachable construction. Named trigger: any future caller that passes `stock=` without `respawn=True` (or vice versa) would desynchronise them, which C#'s single `HasValue` test cannot do.

guards.what: BOOT_UP's Strength scales with the ORIGINAL stock, and 0 is a no-op on both sides
guards.rationale: Axebot.cs:108 is `BootUpStrGain * (2 - StockAmount)` where StockAmount is the construction-time property, not the live StockPower amount; axebot.py:77 is `_BOOT_UP_STR_PER_STOCK * (_DEFAULT_STOCK - self._stock)` off the same stored field. So stock 2 -> 0, stock 1 -> 3, stock 0 -> 6 on both sides, and later respawns come back angrier. The sim's extra `if gain:` guard (axebot.py:78) is not a divergence: C#'s PowerCmd.Apply early-returns on `amount == 0m` (PowerCmd.cs:103), so a 0-Strength application is a no-op there too. The gain-0 case is additionally unreachable, because the stock-2 bot's initial state is HAMMER and BOOT_UP has no in-edges.

BootUpBlock (DeadlyEnemies, 15, 10) -> 10 = _BOOT_UP_BLOCK (axebot.py:13); BootUpStrGain (..., 4, 3) -> 3 = _BOOT_UP_STR_PER_STOCK (:14); OneTwoDamage (..., 10, 9) -> 9 with WithHitCount(2) = :15-16; HammerUppercutDamage (..., 14, 12) -> 12 = :17; WeakPower 2m and FrailPower 2m (Axebot.cs:127-128) = :18-19, applied in that order (axebot.py:88-89). The block carries ValueProp.Move on both sides (Axebot.cs:107, axebot.py:76).

Axebot.cs:127-128 applies Weak/Frail to the move's `targets` collection; axebot.py:88-89 applies them to `ctx.player`. Identical in Ironclad scope -- `targets` is the single player -- and the multiplayer plural is out of scope everywhere.
Read only by GenerateAnimator's initial AnimState choice (Axebot.cs:145). Presentation, and separate from the mechanical `_respawn` flag the sim uses for the initial move.

ONE MECHANISM ACROSS THIS BATCH (rule 3), recorded at every site: the sim's monster ports drop PowerCmd.Apply's `applier` argument. C# is `Apply<T>(choiceContext, target, amount, applier, cardSource)` (PowerCmd.cs:67) and passes `base.Creature` at Axebot.cs:108 (StrengthPower) and :127-128 (Weak/Frail), all applier=base.Creature; note :80 (StockPower) passes null on BOTH sides; the sim's `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, target, power_cls, amount, applier=None)` (cmds.py:271-277) is called without it at axebot.py:79, :88 and :89. In C# a null applier additionally SKIPS the whole Hook.ModifyPowerAmountGiven pass (PowerCmd.cs:123-126) and changes the key FindExistingInstanceForStacking uses (PowerCmd.cs:78, :112). Same observable today, EXECUTED (`py audit/tools/monster_probes_b06.py applier`): the sim has exactly six listener definitions that can see the argument -- powers.py:1172/1181 (ViciousPower, gated `name != "vulnerable" or applier is not self.owner`, powers.py:1167), powers.py:3101/3106 (_PossessPower, gated `applier is self.owner and name == self._stat_id and target.side == "player" and delta < 0`, powers.py:3092-3099), relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-38 (gated on `target is self.player`, never on applier) and relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53 (gated `applier is not self.player`, unsettling_lamp.py:47). None can distinguish `None` from the applying monster for a power this unit applies. Named trigger: porting any listener that reads `applier` positively (a monster-applier-sensitive relic), or porting PowerInstanceType so stacking is keyed by applier. Third-file citations (relics/*.py) not hashed here.
